description: Application to vary condition 1 (Approved Plans) of planning permission Ref: DM2024/01763 for the 'Demolition of existing garages and erection of two attached three storey dwellings with accommodation at basement and loft levels and erection of a three storey side extension at lower ground, ground and first floor level, a part one, part two storey rear extension at basement and ground level, alterations to front, rear and flank fenestrations and increase in roof height including conversion of loft space involving dormer extensions to front, side and rear and rooflights to front and flank roofslopes to provide seven self contained residential units. Provision of private and shared amenity spaces, refuse and cycle stores, car parking spaces, associated landscaping and reduction in width of the vehicular access to and from Elgin Road', to allow for the erection of a single storey rear extension.
decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of planning permission Ref: DM2024/01763 (granted on 3rd April 2025).Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

Details were cleared as part of application CLC2025/00096 on 29.07.2025. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the details approved under application reference CLC2025/00096, completed prior to its occupation/use, and retained thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Details were cleared as part of application CLC2025/00096 on 29.07.2025. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the details approved under application reference CLC2025/00096.Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not interfere with the free flow of traffic and conditions of safety on the public highway, and to ensure the development process does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties in accordance with Policies 29 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Site construction works shall only be carried out between the hours of 0800 and 1800 hours Monday to Friday, 0800 and 1300 hours on Saturday and not at all on Sundays and Bank Holidays.Reason: To protect neighbouring amenities in accordance with policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the occupation of the development, full details of hard and soft landscaping shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All hard and soft landscaping and tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant recommendations of appropriate British Standards (in particular, BS 3882: Specifications for Topsoil, Recommendations (2015) and BS 8545: Trees from Nursery to Independence in the Landscape, Recommendations (2014) or other recognised codes of good practice). The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part or relevant phase of the development or in accordance with the timetable agreed with the Local Planning Authority. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) are removed, die, or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defective shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with others of a similar size/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its consent to any variation.Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonable standard of landscape in accordance with the approved designs in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

All tree(s) on and adjacent to the site shown to be retained shall be protected in accordance with the Arboricultural information submitted with the Application (Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan) and follow recommendations in British Standard BS 5837: Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and Construction - Recommendations (2012). There will be no materials stored within Construction Exclusion Zone (CEZ), and the Tree Protection Fencing (TPF) and other measures shall only be removed on completion of development. On completion of development, the applicant (their heirs or successors in title) shall submit photographic evidence of compliance with BS5837:2012.Reason: To ensure tree(s) significant in terms of their provision of local amenity are protected from construction damage, in accordance with best practice and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of development, an Energy Statement incorporating 'as-designed' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing which demonstrates how each of the proposed dwellings will apply the Mayor's energy hierarchy (use less energy, supply energy efficiently and use renewable energy) to achieve at least a 35% reduction in CO2 emissions below the target emission rate (TER) based on Part L1A of the 2013 Building Regulations and at least a 20% reduction in total emissions (regulated and unregulated) through on-site renewable energy generation. The development should exceed the minimum Part L1A emissions standards through energy efficiency measures alone. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Details were cleared as part of application CLC2025/00096 on 29.07.2025. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details approved under application reference CLC2025/00096 to show that internal potable water consumption for each of the dwellings will be limited to no more than 110 litres per person per day (l/p/d) based on the Government's national calculation method for the purposes of Part G of the Building Regulations.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Surface Water and SuDS Assessment prepared by Base Energy Ltd and dated 24 July 2024. Prior to first occupation of the development, written confirmation that the approved SuDS measures have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Details were cleared as part of application CLC2026/00069 on 24.06.2026. Ground investigation details were accepted under application reference CLC2026/00069.Reason: To reduce flood risk to and from the development in accordance with Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the measures set out in the finalised Basement Impact Assessment (BIA) approved under application reference CLC2026/00069. Prior to first occupation of the dwellings, written confirmation that the approved flood resilience and mitigation measures have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing.Reason: To reduce flood risk to and from the development in accordance with Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, all redundant accesses and crossovers shall be reinstated and returned to a raised kerb, in a manner to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety in accordance with policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first residential occupation of either 33 Clarendon Road or 26 Elgin Avenue, the following details must be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority:a) Scaled plan(s) showing the dimensions of new or amended crossovers adjacent to the application site on Clarendon Road and Elgin Road;b) Scale plan showing the location and dimensions of the accessible parking space for the homes at 33 Clarendon Road;c) Scaled plans and elevations showing the specification and dimensions of the cycle parking provision, including a statement demonstrating compliance with the London Cycling Design Standards.The development must then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained throughout the lifetime of the development.Reasons: To maintain pedestrian and vehicle safety, in accordance with Sutton Local Plan Policy 36; and to encourage sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with London Plan Policy T5 and Sutton Local Plan Policy 37.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Planning Fire Safety Strategy prepared by PD Planning UK (dated 08 December 2024) and supporting drawing reference 3393-46.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.

Development must not be begun unless a biodiversity gain plan (to include management and monitoring) has been submitted to the local planning authority demonstrating how a 10% biodiversity gain can be achieved within the red line of the development site.Reason: To increase biodiversity on the site in accordance with paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework 2024 and Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.
